v6 replaces the single household_size input with allowable_household_size (derived by the IRS default when absent, operator-overridable with a loud warning) and replaces the single age_band with allowable_under_65_count + allowable_65_over_count.

The age-band change fixes a real mispricing: 433-A prints ONE out-of-pocket line for the whole household, so a single age_band would have priced every person at one rate. A household containing anyone 65 or over was being under-allowed.

Allowable household size follows IRS National Standards guidance: generally the persons allowed as dependents on the most recent return, plus the taxpayer and spouse. "Generally" is why the operator override exists.

GROUP TOTALS COUNT PRINTED ROWS ONLY. A total field is the sum of the rows that fit the form; overflow records are dropped and belong on an attachment, so including them would make the printed total disagree with the printed rows. Confirmed as the standing rule.

split._why: The form splits one real-world value across two abutting boxes with hard maxLength limits. Splitting in the engine rather than at intake means ONE HubSpot custom field per real value, not two - and CF names are immutable once provisioned. Consume `chars` source characters per part after applying `strip`; `format` masks the part with # as a digit placeholder. Every part must fit its target's /MaxLen or the fill stops.

_deferred._why: Still unresolved. Validated for existence, never filled. Two Yes/No pairs on page 1 and one on page 2 whose printed question is not yet established.

Their targets appear under `exclusive` so the guard covers them; they carry no checkbox mapping and are never checked.

allowed._why: The IRS USE ONLY / Allowable Expenses column. Only the two lines IRS grants at a FIXED published amount are auto-filled. Everything else in this column is left blank on purpose: a wrong allowable printed on a filed collection statement is worse than an empty cell an examiner fills in. Same rule already proven on 433-F.
allowed._offset_warning: The IRS* field names are offset by one from the printed line they serve. IRS35 is the allowed cell for PRINTED LINE 36, IRS41 for printed line 42, IRS49 for printed line 50, IRS50 for printed line 51. Never bind an allowed target by matching its own number to a line number.
allowed.standards_source: adapters/pdf/maps/433f.standards.json (2026 IRS Collection Financial Standards; form-agnostic despite the 433f prefix - renamed in Commit 1 of this prompt)

national_standards_total.basis: IRS National Standards: "Generally, the total number of persons allowed for National Standards should be the same as those allowed as dependents on the taxpayer's most recent year income tax return." Source: irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/national-standards-food-clothing-and-other-items
national_standards_total.derive_when_absent: 1 (taxpayer) + 1 if marital_status is married + the count of household_members with claimed_on_1040 = yes that fit the printed table. This is what the form itself shows, and it is the IRS default.
national_standards_total.override: If allowable_household_size IS supplied it WINS and is used as given - the IRS wording is "generally", so the operator may depart from the default. Warn loudly, showing both figures, so the departure is recorded rather than silent.
national_standards_total.lookup: National Standards TOTAL for that number of persons, clamped to the published 1-4 range, plus the published per-additional-person amount for each person above 4.

out_of_pocket_health.printed_line: 42 Out of Pocket Health Care Costs
out_of_pocket_health.lookup: (under_65_count x the published under-65 per-person amount) + (65_over_count x the published 65-and-over per-person amount). Read oop_basis from the standards file and STOP if it is not per-person; do not assume.
out_of_pocket_health.why_two_counts: 433-A prints ONE out-of-pocket line for the whole household, unlike 433-F which prints the per-person rate beside separate age-band headcounts. A household can span both age bands, so a single age_band input cannot express it and would silently price an over-65 person at the under-65 rate.
out_of_pocket_health.consistency_check: under_65_count + 65_over_count must equal the household size actually used for the national standards line. Mismatch is a hard stop, not a warning: the two allowed cells would otherwise be computed on different households.
out_of_pocket_health.cross_check: Compare the supplied counts against the ages printed in the household_members table plus the taxpayer and spouse dates of birth where available. Warn on disagreement; do not auto-correct.

_never_autofill._why: Listed as objects, not as object KEYS, so the schema-agnostic validator (which walks string VALUES) checks every one of them for existence. Each is validated and never written.
